short: Large-vocabulary attempted-speech decoding in one participant holds; sensor, decoder and LM are now field standard, but the spiking attribution and cross-study ratios outrun the evidence.
position: The paper changed three components: intracortical arrays in area 6v as the speech sensor (M05), a GRU phoneme decoder trained with CTC (M06), and an online 125,000-word language model (M07). All three are standard against today's ledger because the field adopted them, and a [later] system on the same design reached 2.5% WER on the same vocabulary. The main claim holds as a single-participant demonstration: 23.8% online WER at 62 words per minute on a large vocabulary was new for attempted speech. Crediting spiking resolution for the gain is overreach, since a [concurrent] ECoG system reached a similar error at a higher rate. The 2.7x and 3.4x margins are untested ratios across participants, sensors and tasks, and the online numbers carry no seeds or stated selection data.
